I have absolutely zero interest in EVER speaking to him again. The last time he saw me and the dog he was trying to beat the shit out of us. So essentially I assumed ownership of the dog with little argument from Steven. I don't want to break no contact and bring this traumatizing person back into my life. Not after I've gone so far in improving my self worth. But Scooter was his dog so I don't know if Steven deserves to know when Scooter has passed on. Should I let him say goodbye? AITA for even thinking of putting down a dog that spent so much time not being mine? My normal isn't normal so I really don't know what's okay in this situation. I'm worried because it's getting colder and Scooters arthritis is getting worse. I don't want him to live in pain. Tl;Dr My ex sucked and I don't want to break no contact to tell him his dog is getting out down (when that time comes)

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to put down my ex's dog, Scooter, without telling my ex about it. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Scooter has been with my ex, Steven, for a long time. Steven and I were together, and for about two years, we were the primary caretakers for Scooter. After our breakup, I became Scooter's primary caretaker for the last year. Scooter has arthritis and bad legs, and I'm really worried about his quality of life, especially as it's getting colder. I don't want him to live in pain, so I'm considering putting him down. But here's the thing: Steven is a really volatile and abusive person. He has a history of threatening me and Scooter, being aggressive, and even crashing a car on purpose because I asked him not to drive while drunk. He's been physically abusive, emotionally abusive, and has caused a lot of trauma in my life. Because of this, I have no interest in ever speaking to him again. The last time he saw me and Scooter, he tried to attack us, got blood all over my car, and threatened to hurt both me and Scooter. After that incident, I kicked him out of my life for good. Now, Scooter was his dog, but I've been taking care of him for the past year. I don't know if Steven deserves to know when Scooter passes away. Should I let him say goodbye? On one hand, Scooter was Steven's dog, and he might want to be there for his pet. On the other hand, Steven has caused so much pain and trauma in my life that I don't want to bring him back into it, even for something as final as this. I'm also wondering if it's morally acceptable for me to make the decision to put Scooter down without consulting Steven. Is it my responsibility now, since I've been the primary caretaker? Or should I consider Steven's feelings, even though he's been abusive? Another thing to consider is the well-being of Scooter. If his arthritis is getting worse and he's in pain, is it kinder to put him down rather than let him suffer? I don't want him to live in discomfort, but I also don't want to make a decision that might have long-term consequences for me or others involved. I'm also thinking about the legal aspects. Do I have the right to make this decision alone, or does Steven have any legal claim to Scooter? I'm not sure about the laws in my area regarding pet ownership after a breakup. Additionally, I'm reflecting on my own feelings. I've worked hard to improve my self-worth and move on from the trauma of my relationship with Steven. Bringing him back into my life, even for something as final as this, could be really damaging to my mental health. I don't want to risk undoing all the progress I've made. But then, I also feel guilty for not wanting to tell Steven about Scooter's passing. Is it fair to him to not have closure? Or is it more important to protect myself from further harm? I'm also considering the possibility of finding a middle ground. Maybe I could have someone else inform Steven about Scooter's passing, so I don't have to interact with him directly. That way, Steven gets the information without me having to break my no-contact agreement. However, I'm not sure if that's feasible or if it would cause more problems. Steven might react negatively if he finds out that I didn't tell him directly, even if someone else did. It could lead to more conflict or legal issues. In the end, I'm torn between my responsibility to Scooter's well-being and my need to protect myself from further harm. I want to make the right decision, but I'm not sure what that is.
